handDesc.handNote: Brown main writing and darker interventions are visible. Ink differences are recorded without assigning historical hands.

origin.p: The supplied library manifest dates the manuscript to the 10th/11th century; this does not date individual interventions.

surrogates.p: Library digital facsimile, PPN1844735508. The supplied manifest identifies the images as Public Domain Mark 1.0. Every verse in folios 67v, 68r was inspected for this first pass.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first pass of all 36 manuscript verses. No other witness or normalized edition was used as transcription input. Existing annotation coordinates provide navigation, not text. There are 36 original annotation rows for 36 distinct source verses, without duplicates. Every original rectangle was inspected and retained. Some regions include adjacent text, and additions may lie outside the navigation rectangle. sourceWitness=LL and panelId are provenance only; no other witness text was consulted.

correction.p: Uncertain letters are marked unclear and unreadable text gap. Darker ink is hi, not proof of erasure or a distinct hand. Actual additions use add; deletion or substitution is asserted only with visible evidence and qualified where needed. No unattested earlier reading is supplied.

normalization.p: Single source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs and long s are represented with standard Latin characters. Source spelling is preserved; word spacing and couplet layout are editorial. Explicit abbreviation expansions remain in TEI choices. Punctuation and unusual signs are schematic typographic equivalents, not exact pen-shape replicas.

punctuation.p: Visible significant punctuation and separation or insertion marks are retained. No modern sentence punctuation is supplied.

segmentation.p: Each l is one verse and one physical source line. Full-page inspection of folios67v and68r shows alternate physical verse lines inset; rend on even verses records that source layout. The lg groups are editorial elegiac couplets. Each verse has a stable ID and an existing facsimile rectangle. The rectangles may include neighbouring text and need not enclose marginal inscriptions.

interpretation.p: A different agent independently read all 36 source verses and investigated all 23 first-pass evidence notes. Source-supported decisions were reconciled directly; remaining uncertainty is documented without human-review assignments. The hash-bound review ledger records every note disposition. Independent agent review is not human scholarly approval.

revisionDesc.change: First source pass covering all 36 verses and visible interventions in folios 67v, 68r; awaiting a different agent's independent reading.

Independent source review of all 36 verses and 23 notes completed. All verse readings and source layers are supported at the confidence levels already encoded. No verse changes were necessary. Unusual source spelling, word divisions, additions and conservative uncertainty are preserved. Original zones and source-supported layout remain unchanged; zero human escalations.

div.head: Source evidence after independent review
div.note: The poem begins with a large ornamental C. Omi of pomiferis is dark. The visible following sequence is fore torta; a horizontal stroke crosses the boundary and a vertical mark crosses t. The source components are preserved without imposing a normalized word division or erasure history.
Con is written above before tigimus, and culta above uicta. In comillae, o has a dot below and a above, supporting an expunction/substitution. No cancellation of uicta is asserted.
The final a of Casta is darker. A short horizontal stroke crosses the sacerdotes word division, retained schematically without cancelling the letters.
The source writes Grande more pretium. No normalization of its grammatical form is supplied.
Que after cliuis has darker overlapping strokes and remains qualified. The et ending of prebet is a ligature. The current spelling is retained.
The opening is Stat uetus, with dark final s. Within nubibus, u and the second b are dark. The et conjunction is a ligature. Small oblique marginal marks have unspecified function.
In numenis, a dot beneath e and i above it support an expunction/substitution. Both letters are retained.
The a of praeces is crossed and dotted below; it is retained as del, yielding preces without supplying letters.
A slender vertical stroke follows Ara and crosses the beginning of per. Its function is unspecified.
Hic is written above Hanc. Final a of sollempnia is crossed with a dot below and retained as del. A short stroke also crosses the p-area of presonuit; that mark does not securely cancel p.

Initial I, er of per and first e of uellatas are darker. The a after i before uias is crossed and retained as del. Dots below the uellatas area do not securely establish a cancelled whole word; its readable letters remain uncancelled.

A small c is added above before the final e of iuuene, with a caret beneath. Source e is preserved without normalization to ae. A small dark dot lies near the final r of Ducuntur, but its function is unclear; no cancellation of r is asserted.
The final i of uituli and i of metuendi are darker. Current readings are retained without reconstructing prior letters.
Two dots beneath the final a of cornua indicate expunction. The source ends recuruo, with no final s supplied.
Final a of sola and c of capella are dark and crossed by slender strokes. The readable letters are retained without asserting an erased prior state.
The source reads Praebuerant and iacente. Those forms are retained.
The e of crines is dark; Virginea is retained with its visible ending.

The e of Morem is dark and final m is pale but partly visible; it remains unclear without claiming erasure. Sancto is written above graio. Dots beneath that addition do not securely define cancellation of the baseline word, so both are retained.

The visible sequence after pompae is facie sagamen none caeso. A slender stroke crosses after facie, and a short horizontal stroke follows sagamen. The source wording is retained without restoring a familiar name or missing letters.
A vertical stroke falls between fugit and halesus. Al of halesus is darker. The et conjunction is a ligature; no previous reading is inferred.
Per erratis is editorially separated while retaining the visible source letters.
Final s of faliscos is dark. A paired right-margin stroke is documented without assigning a textual function.
A slender stroke follows mihi. A colon-like mark and terminal stroke precede the large N beginning3.14; the next line is not a heading.
